title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a relative curve with Ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. The symbol \hat S (or \hat Ω on this page) denotes the formal completion along the diagonal, i.e. the ring of infinite jets P^∞_{X/S}. A formal coordinate ω generates the ideal of the diagonal. C is a connection on this jet algebra, C: \hat Ω → \hat Ω ⊗ Ω^1_{X/S}, satisfying the Leibniz rule; it is an Ehresmann/Grothendieck-type connection on the bundle of formal coordinates. The 'normal form' of a projective connection is that C applied to a coordinate is a polynomial of degree ≤ 2 in that coordinate: C(ω) = ϖ_0 + ω ϖ_1 + ω^2 ϖ_2. In modern terms these are the sl_2-type vector fields ∂, z∂, z^2∂, so the horizontal coordinates are defined up to Möbius transformations.

Computation.
(1) For an automorphism u of the formal neighbourhood tangent to the identity to second order, write ω^u = ω(1 + Σ_{i≥2} u_i). The Leibniz rule gives C(ω^u) = C(ω)(1 + Σ u_i) + ω Σ C(u_i).
(2) With λ a function and u_i = α_i ω^i, he gets C(λ ω^i) = ω^i ⊗ dλ + λ i ω^{i-1} C(ω). The first try, with ω = λω_0, is abandoned.
(3) He takes C(ω_0) = ϖ_0 + ω_0 ϖ_1 + ω_0^2 ϖ_2 and computes
 C(ω_0^u) = C(ω_0)(1 + Σ α_i ω_0^i) + ω_0 Σ_{i≥2}(ω_0^i dα_i + i α_i ω_0^{i-1} C(ω_0)).
 This simplifies to
 C(ω_0)(1 + Σ_{i≥2}(i+1) α_i ω_0^i) + ω_0^3 Σ_{i≥2} ω_0^{i-2} ⊗ dα_i,
 which is correct.
(4) He then rewrites the result in the new coordinate ω' = ω_0^u, using ω_0 = ω'/(1 + Σ α_j ω_0^j) as an implicit inversion. The aim is to see when the transformed C is again 'of the form ĉ′', i.e. quadratic in the new coordinate.

What this shows. In the new coordinate the ω^2 coefficient shifts by 3α_2 ϖ_0. So the α_2-part, a section of Ω^{⊗2}, moves the projective connection through the torsor of quadratic differentials; this matches G/G_0 ≅ Γ(Ω^{⊗2}) on the previous page. The higher α_i (i≥3) are forced recursively by killing the coefficients of ω^{i+1}, since ϖ_0 is invertible. This feeds the group-theoretic lemma on the previous and next pages: G_0 × G(c) → G is bijective, i.e. normal forms are unique modulo G_0.

Purpose. The page belongs to establishing the dictionary between projective connections on a curve, projective (PGL_2) structures on formal coordinates, and the affine space of projective connections over quadratic differentials. This is a step toward uniformisation.
errors: In the line for C(λω^i) the bracket reads (ω_{-1} + ω_0 ω ω_1); it should be ω_{-1} + ω ω_0 + ω^2 ω_1, i.e. C(ω), so ω^2 is miswritten or mis-transcribed.

The first attempt C(ω_0^u) = (ϖ_0+ϖ_1+ϖ_2)(1 + Σα_iω_0^i + Σ iα_iω_0^{i-1}) omits the powers of ω_0 on ϖ_1, ϖ_2, the extra factor ω_0 on the second sum, and the dα_i terms. He corrects it immediately in the next computation.

The substitution ω_0 = ω'/(1+Σα_jω_0^j) is only an implicit inversion, since the right side still contains ω_0. Re-expanding C(ω_0) = ϖ_0 + ω_0ϖ_1 + ω_0^2ϖ_2 in ω' also produces higher-order terms, which the struck last line begins to address. The computation is left unfinished but the method is sound.

ideas.what: Transformation law of a connection on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal under coordinate changes ω ↦ ω(1+Σα_iω^i), via the Leibniz rule
ideas.modern_name: Gauge action of Aut O (formal coordinate changes) on flat connections on the Aut O-torsor of formal coordinates (Gelfand–Kazhdan formal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gelfand–Kazhdan (1971); Beilinson–Drinfeld; Frenkel–Ben-Zvi (Vertex Algebras and Algebraic Curves)
ideas.where_published: The connection on jets / formal neighbourhood of the diagonal appears in Grothendieck's crystalline work (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, Dix exposés) and EGA IV §16; the projective-connection application is not known to be published

ideas.what: Normal form C(ω) = ϖ_0 + ωϖ_1 + ω^2ϖ_2, with C quadratic in the coordinate, characterising projective connections; the freedom is α_2 ∈ Γ(Ω^{⊗2})
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures / sl_2-opers; space of projective connections as an affine space over quadratic differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarzian derivative); Gunning (1966); Deligne (1970) for the algebraic setting; Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Leibniz-rule computation of how a quadratic-normal-form connection changes under formal coordinate changes. It is part of a standard argument that projective connections form a torsor under quadratic differentials. The Grothendieck-style jet-connection framing anticipates Gelfand–Kazhdan / opers language, but nothing beyond known results appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'C(ω) = ωω_{-1} + ωω_0 + ωω_1' is more plausibly C(ω) = ω_{-1} + ωω_0 + ω^2ω_1 (coefficient forms ω_i ∈ \hat Ω⊗Ω^1); the transcription's leading ω's are likely misreadings.
'Ω^{⊗ i}' under the first line is likely ω^{⊗i}, i.e. powers of the coordinate ω, introducing the next formula.
In 'C(ω_0^u) = ... (ϖ_0+ϖ_1+ϖ_2)', the struck prefix is 'C(ω_0' and the superscript on the last sum appears to be i-1.
